#
Dear Friend,

Every 80 seconds, a preborn child loses its life at the hands of Planned Parenthood. This means that by the time you finish reading this email, another innocent life will be gone.

Despite the Supreme Court ruling in the overturning of _Roe v. Wade_ , Planned Parenthood continues to receive taxpayer funding, effectively subsidizing the intentional killing of preborn children. Since 2000, nearly $10.7 billion of taxpayers' money has funded their life-ending work.

Contrast this with the nearly 3,000 Pro-life pregnancy centers nationwide dedicated to supporting expectant mothers. Planned Parenthood only operates about 600 facilities and primarily offers one service: abortion. Alarmingly, they perform 62 abortions for every prenatal care service they provide, and prenatal care services are down 80% since 2010.

As a pro-life individual, I know you don't want your hard-earned tax dollars to support an organization that prioritizes abortion.

That's why I'm urging you to join us to demand an end to this taxpayer-funded ongoing tragedy. A new Congress and president will be chosen this November, and they need to hear from us _now_ that America does NOT support funding Planned Parenthood.

Make your voice heard. Sign our petition before midnight to demand an end to this grave misuse of your taxes. **[https://www.liveaction.org/defund-planned-parenthood-petition/](http://links.redconservatives.com/u/click?_t=66ce1250519441959ebe70cf27686494&_m=1dc7a312cea9425c9f5a247cac355965&_e=57YLHvelPvBQxlC40xBmHhordIUkMme3TwXxfVxcMrxdCGlvbLpqDKYODUsEyjpVMu9zCMbCvzwAXXYZvJ60-hIP0GI1DOSPBXdJU2c95yOPX-R51V4Nrr1VsOZHcd3vf1ivG0kWjrBpc4-k4DbiX3kgoZuuICeTnB9XjLbJMuAWMQIOY2mFugVjQAM1XKJfUOtFyBzsIo-G-f_5QBMmJsJPAv-9LuQicC3dhpbcqkn3cL-1fAlQSIxHt8SIgSQnNoDdQdcGxi2aIiWeKCPrxGJO0zXOn0iCyFcb-Eykdot9MBceOn9L2CTOaXUst4hybBInlNGEPOYPut4ea4vzHHmSjGat6LggI1TPE0d3llX5YoZssobUka9x3zb35SyuoFK5-VdyIPuH7XvuoczdtQ%3D%3D)**

Thank you for standing with us for the protection of future generations!

For Life,

Lila Rose

| | | [](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=df1e7b2538d8407bbc7035898e16efe3&_e=05wKqDwX6Mioj0HB1j_Sadv5L4nq9-aAyn3bKXbYtwrsSsQBe8fuTJ6soA1wSrzjAtyL4S88xgUgBnWd_2xFOErWfh2sZ4VLdYeZ7wzS-SqeOzYiRtRI0inJKhjRPA9-giFi4JEFXNiqqJevh-zlVxjBnoa8X-rMPEqY-9tgSfHt0vh1F4qzbNBN37TK3ezqp1rO2qa0nxo_CgQMEr2DKhEVzJ1TlkiQtCGNGeL7TueZqDadoFnUtox7T3HaECg4Q3vuBEz2dGAymaCt_0oz69L0GwXJ6hTAOa5wovFaUSwHk1VH4p1CW2Xoqv4lSKWtfmM7pKxCAE7_rNUd8AZdLrQxZI1vzBMWV8ZeFOMdpKnDzQzVL9Lpc2JHgIXCRY9PgFAulRH7AwP-yxviOOFA5688_6bQHyKG3GY1lnhFNxw%3D)
---
| Fellow Patriot,

I feel like our culture has forgotten--or ignored--some very important and basic lessons when it comes to the development of human life.

Our society has been infected by an anti-life ideology, treating its most vulnerable members as disposable objects. Abortion that was once thought of as a last resort in a medical emergency has become the new normal.

Medicine tells us that life begins at the moment of conception. It also tells us when an unborn baby develops a heartbeat, brainwaves, and nervous system. Yet, despite all of this, the unborn are not treated as though they are alive or even human. [](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=df1e7b2538d8407bbc7035898e16efe3&_e=05wKqDwX6Mioj0HB1j_Sadv5L4nq9-aAyn3bKXbYtwrsSsQBe8fuTJ6soA1wSrzjAtyL4S88xgUgBnWd_2xFOErWfh2sZ4VLdYeZ7wzS-SqeOzYiRtRI0inJKhjRPA9-giFi4JEFXNiqqJevh-zlVxjBnoa8X-rMPEqY-9tgSfHt0vh1F4qzbNBN37TK3ezqp1rO2qa0nxo_CgQMEr2DKhEVzJ1TlkiQtCGNGeL7TueZqDadoFnUtox7T3HaECg4Q3vuBEz2dGAymaCt_0oz6x9-jxxikElk6qnEf9m9X8flFPRZRm96JMMec0LqTBmvQg7r31koiEoaem9R5x3H_cBKExwyjMH7ybkfh6MHP1UugGGKhDWWN3aEvesXPVAGedT_3HQNiAhzaha4ZZYDmR-CByoQd10djjOfnxc0V4Y%3D) **As a surgeon, I have operated on infants pre-birth. I can assure you that they are very much alive.**

Life is a precious gift that has been given to us from our creator. No person is disposable, and every life is precious according to Him.

I believe that everyone deserves life, even those who have been denied this right by our society. I believe that together we can make a difference and bring dignity and a voice to the unborn. I also believe that I'm not alone in this belief.

I believe that you believe that too.

I've started working with a group of like-minded individuals who are looking to change our culture. We want to build a society that values life but that takes people like you and I making a commitment.

The first step is clearly stating what we believe and what we are willing to do to protect the lives of the unborn. **[**Will you join me today and stand up for those who cannot do it for themselves?**](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=df1e7b2538d8407bbc7035898e16efe3&_e=05wKqDwX6Mioj0HB1j_Sadv5L4nq9-aAyn3bKXbYtwrsSsQBe8fuTJ6soA1wSrzjAtyL4S88xgUgBnWd_2xFOErWfh2sZ4VLdYeZ7wzS-SqeOzYiRtRI0inJKhjRPA9-giFi4JEFXNiqqJevh-zlVxjBnoa8X-rMPEqY-9tgSfHt0vh1F4qzbNBN37TK3ezqp1rO2qa0nxo_CgQMEr2DKhEVzJ1TlkiQtCGNGeL7TueZqDadoFnUtox7T3HaECg4Q3vuBEz2dGAymaCt_0oz6yrmaFcJYXxVKk0xw4iiu8j2Ss_njMkF2k_imDGzb0FzQX0g7NA_abUMUSZa8nYBkImqPL-N9S8gj-pTqsG322IL2OmcnmU-M4v7HGYhPey7ecrke_PkTBhZUp0riJyKTpLrJK5o08l9XQyPNvyy4yI%3D)**

I've created a new pro-life pledge; I'd love your support. Would you read the pledge below to see if you align with our shared goals and are willing to commit to fighting for the lives of the unborn?

[https://offers.americancornerstone.org/pro-life-statement/](http://links.liberty-pulse.com/u/click?_t=29bc9815846f49728b1d374165de7bf2&_m=df1e7b2538d8407bbc7035898e16efe3&_e=05wKqDwX6Mioj0HB1j_Sadv5L4nq9-aAyn3bKXbYtwrsSsQBe8fuTJ6soA1wSrzjAtyL4S88xgUgBnWd_2xFOErWfh2sZ4VLdYeZ7wzS-SqeOzYiRtRI0inJKhjRPA9-giFi4JEFXNiqqJevh-zlVxjBnoa8X-rMPEqY-9tgSfHt0vh1F4qzbNBN37TK3ezqp1rO2qa0nxo_CgQMEr2DKhEVzJ1TlkiQtCGNGeL7TueZqDadoFnUtox7T3HaECg4Q3vuBEz2dGAymaCt_0oz64h7DTq29ENFbM4me2-YQQyrIJHTypMlfIGj5whmaNO0kMkOwSmqaxCnWg2xreYloBEhtIqRVouosaT0be__NBwc4nLovq-S6BS-NA7sgSMg3Aiuht_wilKgh9lRtyYGOsn403c-_G-IHosPZeCMEY8%3D)

If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | | | | Fellow Patriot, I feel like our culture has forgotten--or ignored--some very important and basic lessons when it comes to the development of human life. Our society has been infected by an anti-life ideology, treating its most vulnerable members as disposable objects. Abortion that was once thought of as a last resort in a medical emergency has become the new normal. Medicine tells us that life begins at the moment of conception. It also tells us when an unborn baby develops a heartbeat, brainwaves, and nervous system. Yet, despite all of this, the unborn are not treated as though they are alive or even human. As a surgeon, I have operated on infants pre-birth. I can assure you that they are very much alive. Life is a precious gift that has been given to us from our creator. No person is disposable, and every life is precious according to Him. I believe that everyone deserves life, even those who have been denied this right by our society. I believe that together we can make a difference and bring dignity and a voice to the unborn. I also believe that I'm not alone in this belief. I believe that you believe that too. I've started working with a group of like-minded individuals who are looking to change our culture. We want to build a society that values life but that takes people like you and I making a commitment. The first step is clearly stating what we believe and what we are willing to do to protect the lives of the unborn. I've created a new pro-life pledge; I'd love your support. name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: Before Trump takes the stage again in MI tomorrow...
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1934%2E135344%2EjOLsSq)

Friend --
Trump will be Michigan again tomorrow for his first visit since the presidential debate -- his 10th visit since of his 2024 presidential campaign. JD Vance will also be here, on the west side of the state.
**I am asking for a contribution -- $3 or whatever you can afford -- before Donald Trump takes the stage tomorrow. If that's all you need to hear, please use this link to donate today:**
**[https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/-Trump-Visit](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-sep24.1Cpmdt&refcode=em240916-2-900&t=2&akid=1934%2E135344%2EjOLsSq)**
Here's how former President Trump's visit plays in our race:
We know that both the presidential race and the Senate majority will be decided by Michigan – and recent polls show that our race is a dead heat.
Given that the Senate race is the top of the ticket in the state, we know that whatever happens in our race will impact the presidential, too. That’s why Trump has given Mike Rogers his full-throated endorsement -- and why he’s attacked me directly, by name, calling me a “far-left liberal lunatic.” We expect to hear that and more tomorrow, unfortunately.
He knows that in order to win Michigan, the Republican nominee needs to win the Senate race – and he’s going to do whatever he can to make that happen.
That means we can likely expect to see Trump in Michigan a lot more in the stretch. National Republicans will be doing everything they can to flip our state red and boost our ultimate GOP opponent in the Senate race. In fact, outside groups have already spent more than $17 million in attack ads against me on TV — and we know more are on the way.
If we are going to keep this seat blue in November, we need to hold the line by keeping our own positive TV ads on the air, doubling down on our field outreach, and continuing to meet voters in every corner of the state.
[**Trump will be here tomorrow. It would be a huge boon to our campaign if you would chip in and show your support before he gets here. Our goal is to send a message that we are NOT letting them win back Michigan! Even a single $5 or $10 contribution goes a long way when lots of folks are chipping in.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-sep24.1Cpmdt&refcode=em240916-2-900&t=3&akid=1934%2E135344%2EjOLsSq)

name: David Pan
subject: Increasing government spending only makes our problems worse
disclaimer_text: paid for by everyone else
body:
Two visions of the future

| | | | | [](https://eot.davidpanforcongress.com/f/a/dzl3ltqkPuPum-SsRazGeA~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRoyvPFP0UgYjMwODlhYTM4MTlkMWJlOTM3MWE5OGVhMzRkZDU2MmREImh0dHA6Ly93d3cuZGF2aWRwYW5mb3Jjb25ncmVzcy5jb21XBXNwY2V1Qgpmz8Vu6GZGJT0yUhRkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbVgEAABrnQ~~)
---
| | The typical Democratic Party playbook for elections consists in paying off certain groups of voters with proposals such as: no tax on tips, tax deductions for down payments on a home, new child tax credits, and student loan forgiveness.

All of these proposals have three things in common that speak against them.

First, they each favor a specific group of people – restaurant workers, new home buyers, new parents, college graduates – with a giveaway that will have to be paid for by everyone else. For instance, the down payment tax deduction will increase demand for homes without increasing supply and thereby push overall home prices even higher.

Second, by creating a specific class of people to receive benefits, such giveaways will encourage fraudulent claims. We saw this phenomenon with the COVID policies on unemployment insurance, which resulted in an estimated $100 billion in payments to fraudsters.

Third, these proposals all involve increased government spending and will result in even more national debt, which is already spiraling out of control at the rate of almost $2 trillion per year, while revenues amount to only $4.4 trillion per year. This ballooning debt will lead to more inflation and economic collapse if it is not brought under control.

I have a different plan.

Instead of passing out money to favored groups, I want to reduce government spending first and then reward everyone for such restraint by both reducing the budget deficit and returning money to citizens equally. We can do this by phasing out the entire welfare and entitlement system, which currently costs $4 trillion per year, so that we can return this money to citizens as a $16,000 per year universal basic income (or universal tax credit) that, in my plan, would amount to $3 trillion per year on a steady state basis after transition costs. This $3 trillion per year would not be an expense but part of the savings produced by first cutting government spending by $4 trillion per year. The other $1 trillion per year saved can be used to reduce our budget deficit and fund transition costs.

Because our current system creates specific classes of people to receive payments, we spur people to use their ingenuity to game the system. My plan puts money back into everyone’s hands equally and relies on free markets in which businesses would offer what currently is being provided by the government. By dissolving the government monopoly on services such as health care and retirement insurance, my plan encourages people to start businesses to provide services in the most cost-effective way possible. This new system has little room for fraud and would reward people for using their ingenuity to provide value to consumers.

You can find more details about my plan at [DavidPanforCongress.com](https://eot.davidpanforcongress.com/f/a/A7pxZWACfwhDHFFuE7H1Wg~~/AAAHUQA~/RgRoyvPFP0UgOTAxMzZkNDExNGNjNTI1ZGVlNzFmNDc5NGU5ZTYwZGREHmh0dHA6Ly9EYXZpZFBhbmZvckNvbmdyZXNzLmNvbVcFc3BjZXVCCmbPxW7oZkYlPTJSFGRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tWAQAAGud). Please help to get the word out by forwarding this message to friends, family, and neighbors. You can also meet me at my upcoming fundraiser in Santa Ana at 5 pm on September 25. RSVP at [info@davidpanforcongress.com](mailto:info@davidpanforcongress.com) for more information. Together, we can save our country from useless government spending and return this money to the people.

subject: Here's how we unrig Washington

body:
https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]

Friend,

It's time to unrig Washington. Too many legislators are beholden to corporate money, and a politicized Supreme Court remains dangerously out of step with our nation’s highest ideals.

First the ask: Will you rush a $3 donation to my campaign right now if you agree? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/anti-corruption-fundraiser?refcode=20240916&amount=3]

DONATE $3 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/anti-corruption-fundraiser?refcode=20240916&amount=3]

I’ve introduced a political reform package to unrig Washington and strengthen our democracy:

✅ Ban campaign contributions from PACs and lobbyists of any kind;
✅ Ban stock trading by members of Congress and lobbying by retired members;
✅ Set 12-year term limits for members of Congress;
✅ Set 18-year term limits for Supreme Court justices; and
✅ Implement a judicial code of ethics for federal judges and Supreme Court justices

Restoring confidence in our democratic institutions requires us to show that we’re putting the American people first, not corporations, or special interests.

When I was elected to Congress, the first thing I did was start the No PAC Caucus. I still refuse to take a dime of lobbyist, corporate PAC, or any PAC money. But Congress will not voluntarily give up their addiction to big money.

We need to show them there is overwhelming grassroots demand for a different kind of politics. Can I count on your support? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/anti-corruption-fundraiser?refcode=20240916]

Just as my vision for a new economic patriotism aims to improve the living standards of all Americans, this platform is designed to build a better democracy for every American.

Your $3 donation today is the best way to show my fellow Democrats why they need to support bold platforms to unrig Washington.

Onward,
Ro

Imagine if the cost of producing bullshit is zero. And then apply that to all of the bad actors out in the world. That’s what AI is going to enable.

---
| [](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.QtKflUKrzodfXtago74Ps8EN3ROWxEkMkeIirpafo0UGJ4pTT-5OuiTmqb8f15eNO_tJeu6Yxj4LFXkgkQqvPHfMte9lnflQotEopy6o_Y7swJeA0I3Ek0QbGlvN7_pmsN-zUNjKS3U97Kcskt3_9_SWd2d8-rDjGgpCYW6WqOMi7zy2IY6YK-U0D5sRbLugN6FuLxFrRySvILo4ep4cn_1Uk86C0YTDVdFwp7KACmo/49t/5n2nnw7RQx6Ick3MQf7P4A/h0/h001.A4LtPP9V4iPt2fRBmrTG0ykO4KJrgb7oijlY1dC_tfU)

Hello, I hope that your Fall is going great.
4 years ago I ran for President in large part on the impending arrival of AI and what it would mean. This week I spent time with Tristan Harris and Aza Raskin, the co-founders of the Center for Humane Technology. You might know them from the Netflix documentary “The Social Dilemma.” Said Tristan this week, “As a society we had a hands-off approach to social media, and there have been any number of negative effects. Hopefully we’ve learned our lesson with AI, which will be an even more dramatic and transformative technology.” They believe that government should be taking a greater role in mitigating the potential pitfalls of AI.
Also in that camp is Gary Marcus, whom I interview on the podcast this week. Gary is a professor and experienced technologist who started an AI company that was acquired by Uber. “I think that AI could improve our way of life in many ways, making us healthier and unlocking major scientific breakthroughs. But I also think there are real risks that are with us here and now.” Gary breaks down these risks in his new book, “Taming Silicon Valley: How We Can Ensure AI Works for Us.”
“AI could lead to a collapse in trust that could easily jeapordize democracy,” Gary says. “Imagine if the cost of producing bullshit is zero. And then apply that to all of the bad actors out in the world. That’s what AI is going to enable.” This is both personal and societal, as we can all be subject to audio calls and messages that sound like loved ones having an emergency but are really AI looking to scam us out of our money. Meanwhile, one can imagine countries being misled into hostilities based on bad info propagated by foreign actors.
Gary is concerned about bias baked into the algorithms. “AI is increasingly being used for hiring decisions. Imagine if certain classes or types of people are locked out of opportunities algorithmically and there’s nothing they can do. Meanwhile people using the algorithms for hiring would barely understand how they work.”
Of course, AI could change the very nature of work. “Are there jobs that will be made obsolete by AI? Yes there are,” Gary asserts. “We need a different way for the public to benefit from AI than our current tax system and a new way for people to share in that value.” Gary favors piloting income and cash transfer programs to help ease what will be an historic transition.
I’m personally very confident that AI is going to eat through many American jobs; just the other day I spoke to someone who said they used to have 15 designers suggesting various ideas for graphics and clothing. They recently fired them all because now they use AI for the same task. A lot of creative work is being changed to utilize AI, which often means fewer workers. What 4 years ago was hypothetical is now immediate.
One thing I like about Gary is that he’s no bystander; he’s already testified to the Senate about AI and is agitating for better policy. “That’s why I wrote this book, out of frustration and a deep desire to help us get this right.” He proposes a number of policies, including data rights, layered AI oversight and meaningful tax reform that would help.
It probably doesn’t surprise you that I agree with Gary’s call to action. AI is here and changing the nature of our reality and how we interact with the world. Left to its own devices there will be some major downsides. If we want more of the good and less of the bad, it will be up to us and our leaders. Time is of the essence. AI gets smarter and more powerful every day, while we are lucky to stay about the same.

name: Mal Hyman for Congress
subject: There's no debate: this week reminds us why American leadership matters
body:
23 years post-9/11, America's greatest threat lost his mind behind a debate podium

View this email in your browser (https://us21.campaign-archive.com/?e=5d7e9a146c&u=98998055a4d4c8cdda41af3ea&id=9f41a16bb0)

** There’s no debate: American leadership matters
------------------------------------------------------------

**
------------------------------------------------------------

Lost in the midst of a tense presidential election cycle sits a solemn day - September 11th - earlier this week marking 23 years since our nation and its course was forever changed.

Like many of you, I went about that morning as I’d done many before - settling in at work, only to find myself, my students and fellow Coker College faculty drawn to watching a horrific scene unfold on nearby television screens. In a matter of hours, we lost nearly three thousand fellow Americans to a gruesome coordinated terror attack - the worst of its kind ever on American soil.

The shock, the grief and yes, the anger steeled our collective resolve to unite as “one nation” to bring justice to those behind that heinous day’s terror. That unity surely sent shivers down the spines of our enemies, as fleeting as it then was.

It’s that sense of “unity” this nation must return to. Instead, we were led into two costly, deadly and unnecessary wars.

The lives we lost that day, and on battlefields before and after it, cannot have been lost in vain. Those memories should steel our resolve to do better; to be better.

Tuesday night, like many of you, I watched as the two options we have to lead this nation made their pitches, and like many of you, I came away both gobsmacked and awestruck. Gobsmacked that anyone believes Donald Trump should be within shouting distance of the Oval Office again and awestruck by the calm and determined resolve shown by Vice President Kamala Harris. While Trump name-dropped brutal dictators like Viktor Orban, Harris touted our strengthened alliances with NATO nation members. While Trump vowed to cave to Vladimir Putin on day one, Harris pledged to stand with Ukraine; and while we’re on the subject of 9/11 ... it was Trump who literally said “I got involved with the Taliban.”

His rationale?

“The Taliban was killing our soldiers; a lot of them... I got involved ... because the Taliban was doing the killing.”

A former commander-in-chief admitted he sought to negotiate with a terror organization in response to their attacking our men and women in uniform. That alone should be disqualifying. The resulting calamity of our exit and the casualties suffered at Abbey Gate can be traced back to his awful choice to “get involved with the Taliban.”

Vice President Kamala Harris clearly won Tuesday night’s debate and, God willing, will be elected President on November 5th; but Donald Trump did provide us the reminder we needed when it comes to what’s down the ballot, too.

Codifying ‘Roe v Wade’ won’t be possible, without a Congress in Democratic control. Strengthening the Affordable Care Act won’t be possible without Democrats holding the Senate, and taking back the House, either. Seeing to it that Putin is defeated ... that a ceasefire in Gaza is reached ... that our education system is well-funded and staffed ... that college is affordable ... that small business can prosper and that Americans take home a living wage ... none of it’s possible without controlling the House, the Senate and the White House in the hands of those who bring ideas instead of those who seek to obstruct those ideas.

When I’m in Congress, on a multitude of issues, I’ll have Kamala Harris and Tim Walz’ backs. WIll you join the fight and have my back?

That “unity” we felt on September 12 nearly 23 years ago today is - I believe - closer than ever before. Republicans - many who were in office that day - have joined our cause to prevent a second Trump presidency. This November - up and down the ballot - we need a once-in-a-generational outcome.

Are you with us?

Friend, when I first met Kirsten Gillibrand, she was a young lawyer running for Congress in a district with more cows than Democrats.
Defeating a deeply entrenched GOP incumbent in a tough red district is no easy task. Truthfully, there weren't many people who thought she could pull it off. **But on election night in 2006, people everywhere learned to never — _ever_ — count Kirsten out.** (For the record, I'm proud to be one of her earliest believers.)
Since that first election, Kirsten has proven herself time and time again as a fierce, bold advocate for families around America. The minute she was sworn in as our junior senator, I gained an incredible partner. During our time serving in the Senate, we've worked together on countless pieces of legislation, secured millions in federal funding for vital social programs and proudly fought for progress as a united team.
**As Kirsten's colleague and friend —** _and as our Senate majority_** **_leader_**— take it from me: We need Kirsten's voice in the Senate.** But following a red wave in New York in 2022, Republicans are already targeting her seat for defeat.

As her midnight deadline rapidly approaches, we need all hands on deck. That's why I'm personally reaching out. [Please, friend, will you donate $5 or more right now to help defend Kirsten's must-win seat? _" I grew up as the 9th of 10 children in Greensboro. My father was an alcoholic who beat my mother. He died when I was in the fifth grade, and I was terrified. He had been the sole provider for our household. I remember sitting on the porch wondering where I'd be in five years.

Would I be in a shelter? In foster care? Would I be separated from my brothers and sisters?

A few days after my father died, my mom's friend came by. She explained that now that her husband was gone, _my mother could kick her feet up and relax because the government would take care of everything._

_" I grew up as the 9th of 10 children in Greensboro. My father was an alcoholic who beat my mother. He died when I was in the fifth grade, and I was terrified. He had been the sole provider for our household. I remember sitting on the porch wondering where I'd be in five years.

Would I be in a shelter? In foster care? Would I be separated from my brothers and sisters?

A few days after my father died, my mom's friend came by. She explained that now that her husband was gone, _my mother could kick her feet up and relax because the government would take care of everything._

**But that wasn 't my mom. **

As soon as her friend left, she got up and walked over to the local university and got a job as a janitor. She had a fifth-grade education and five kids to provide for. She chose to clean up for other kids to provide for her own. **She didn 't just rise to the challenge, she excelled.**"_
Mark Robinson is North Carolina's first black lieutenant governor running to be the first black governor of North Carolina. This race is adding up to be nearly $80 MILLION in television ads. That doesn't include the attacks liberals will launch by mail, by phone, and by radio ads!

body:
Trump survives another assassination attempt, plus an electric night at the Rumble
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**September 16, 2024** **SPECIAL REPORT** **By Heidi Ganahl**
| | Dear Readers,
In a weekend shadowed by distressing events, the resolve and unity of Colorado’s conservative community have never been more pronounced. Our community came together at the Rocky Mountain Rumble in Sedalia, Colorado last night, an event that turned into more than just a gathering—it became a statement of resilience and unity in the face of adversity.
Just hours before our gathering, former President Donald Trump was subjected to [ANOTHER assassination attempt](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) at his golf course in Florida. The [alleged assailant](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), identified as Ryan Wesley Routh, was apprehended after a tense confrontation, ensuring no harm came to Mr. Trump. This incident marks the second such attempt on the former president in just 65 days, escalating concerns over his safety and the stark political divisions marking our times.
Back in Sedalia, the atmosphere was electrified by speeches from Colorado's strongest conservative voices like Congresswoman Lauren Boebert, who donned a “Bulletproof Trump 2024” shirt, speaking on her unwavering support for the former president amidst these trials. I then spoke of the critical juncture we face in history, urging all to organize and engage in local elections to uphold our values and secure our political future -- a topic I'll be doing a press conference on later this week.
The event also spotlighted pressing local concerns, such as the violence associated with the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, with Aurora City Councilwoman Danielle Jurinsky and CD 6 candidate John Fabbricatore. Valdamar Archuleta, candidate for HD1 in Denver, and Sergei Matveyuk, candidate for Colorado’s 7th district, shared their campaigns' focus on direct and meaningful engagement with voters while fighting to protect the American dream.
As we navigate these turbulent times, let's continue to support those who represent our values and work towards a future where safety and liberty are guaranteed for all.
A huge thanks for all our volunteers who were at the event last night! We're building a movement and can't thank YOU all enough for joining us as we give a voice to conservatives in Colorado. Want to get involved? [Click here and write "Volunteer with RMV" in the message box!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)

Stay informed, stay engaged, and most importantly, stay united.
Warm regards, Heidi Ganahl

Despite high disapproval for President Joe Biden in red states like Kentucky and Mississippi, Democrats outperformed their party’s presidential margin in statewide races by double digits. And after Republican-dominated legislatures passed extreme abortion bans in red states like Kansas and Ohio, voters delivered huge wins for reproductive rights and democracy.
But the truth is, this isn’t all that new. While pundits and insiders increasingly divide us into columns of red and blue based on their one-dimensional view of politics, voters continue to confound their expectations in election after election.
Missouri is a great example. While our state has shifted solidly red in presidential preferences since 2012, Democrats have won a half-dozen statewide campaigns, even as recently as 2018. And when Missouri politicians have adopted extreme positions on issues such as abortion, workers’ rights or health care, they’ve often seen their out-of-touch agendas soundly rejected by voters.
**Just like voters in states where we’ve seen big wins for Democrats and pro-freedom initiatives in the past year, hundreds of thousands of voters in Missouri are still splitting their tickets.**
I know this more than most because I’ve lived it. I won a race for Missouri Secretary of State. And in 2016, Missouri’s last Senate race to take place during a presidential election, I fell just 2.8% short of defeating a longtime Republican incumbent for U.S. Senate. And I outperformed the Democratic presidential ticket’s margin by more than 16%.
We proved that in races where well-funded candidates can set themselves apart and make it clear to voters that they’ll fight for them in office, Democrats can win in Missouri.
That’s what we’re seeing in Missouri’s current U.S. Senate race, as my friend Lucas Kunce takes on incumbent Josh Hawley. Much like my race in 2016, 2024 pits a labor-backed veteran against a politician — _except my opponent never tried to overthrow the government violently just to get his name out there._
Now up for reelection in 2024, Hawley faces Lucas, a Marine veteran and antitrust advocate who’s broken fundraising records, rallied Missouri’s election-winning labor movement behind him and built a reputation as a different kind of Democrat who speaks truth to power, regardless of party.
**[I’m proud to support Lucas Kunce in his race against Josh Hawley and I hope you’ll join me by adding a donation of $10 or whatever you’re able to today. Multiple polls have already confirmed that this will be a tight race, so your early support could be what helps Lucas tip the scales.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/71964?refcode=em20240916-7683&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=10&akid=7683%2E614464%2E-PdJN9)**

**Now let’s talk about why Josh Hawley is so vulnerable.**
Hawley famously popped popcorn in his dorm room to gleefully watch the invasion of Iraq and then claimed a decade later to have opposed the war.
And since he’s represented Missouri in the U.S. Senate, he’s also become known as a desperately anti-union scab who is self-consciously obsessed with manhood.
From blocking defense nominations to voting against health care for veterans exposed to burn pits, Hawley has put his personal politics ahead of national security and the needs of military families. And he’s used his office to build a family business dedicated to restricting abortion access nationwide as his allies in Jefferson City enacted one of the nation’s most extreme abortion bans.
**Now with five years under Hawley’s belt in the U.S. Senate, Missourians don’t like what they’ve seen.**
Approval polling from _Morning Consult_ shows that Hawley has the lowest approval of any GOP senator running for reelection in 2024, lower than Sens. Ted Cruz of Texas and Rick Scott of Florida. And even his mentor, Missouri’s former U.S. Sen. John Danforth, has called backing Hawley the _“worst mistake I ever made.”_
Donald Trump recently commented on Hawley’s race too — _“So interesting that the Democrats are looking hard at the Senate races in both Missouri and Texas. Josh and Ted must be very careful, stranger things have happened!!!”_
**Hawley is vulnerable, and everyone knows it.** The proof is in his rapidly changing election-season rhetoric, Republicans in Washington fretting about their draconian abortion bans across the country, and Hawley’s billionaire allies launching a new pro-Hawley super PAC right after Lucas entered the race.

_" I grew up as the 9th of 10 children in Greensboro. My father was an alcoholic who beat my mother. He died when I was in the fifth grade, and I was terrified. He had been the sole provider for our household. I remember sitting on the porch wondering where I'd be in five years.

Would I be in a shelter? In foster care? Would I be separated from my brothers and sisters?

**But that wasn 't my mom. **

**Nella Domenici**
Republican for Senate

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

Yet politicians like Kevin Cramer do nothing to fix it – it’s infuriating.
That’s why I’m running to replace Kevin Cramer who accepts money from pharmaceutical companies and votes AGAINST lowering prescription drug prices for our seniors.
[**_But I need your help to get to Washington where I will fight tooth and nail to deliver for everyday Americans – like you. I need 415 gifts before midnight to fund my people-powered campaign and compete with Cramer’s deep pockets. Can you rush $15 before midnight to help? Anything you can spare makes a world of difference. >>_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92944719/498827222/-1408912288?amount=15&refcode=20240916_em_fr_b1_katrina_main_rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg4ODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTljNTg0M2YtNWY3NC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=RIxixTkJMuakm4rhv3_VoW0EsfFq_ueX5mxMrQs7m2c=)
[**People like my parents.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92944723/498827226/-1408912288?amount=15&refcode=20240916_em_fr_b1_katrina_main_rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg4ODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTljNTg0M2YtNWY3NC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=RIxixTkJMuakm4rhv3_VoW0EsfFq_ueX5mxMrQs7m2c=) They worked hard to provide for us as they struggled to get by in rural America.
They counted on food stamps to put dinner on the table.
They counted on government-funded programs, like Headstart to put me in Preschool.
So believe me when I say, I understand the struggle millions of families face.
[**But I’m up against Republican Kevin Cramer who has only voted to slash funding from federal programs struggling families rely on and funnels special interest cash into his campaign coffers. **](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92944726/498827230/-1408912288?amount=15&refcode=20240916_em_fr_b1_katrina_main_rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg4ODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTljNTg0M2YtNWY3NC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=RIxixTkJMuakm4rhv3_VoW0EsfFq_ueX5mxMrQs7m2c=)
[**_Peter – I will never forget where I came from or who I am fighting for in the Senate. But first, I have to compete with Cramer’s millionaire and billionaire mega-donors. I’m not taking a dime of Corporate PAC money – so to fund this groundbreaking campaign, I’m counting on your help. I need 415 gifts before midnight to build an unstoppable foundation of support, win this competitive race, and finally send Cramer packing for good. Will you chip in $15 before midnight? >>_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92944728/498827233/-1408912288?amount=15&refcode=20240916_em_fr_b1_katrina_main_rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg4ODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTljNTg0M2YtNWY3NC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=RIxixTkJMuakm4rhv3_VoW0EsfFq_ueX5mxMrQs7m2c=)

One without gun violence, soaring student loan debt, and inaction toward climate change.
I know I’m not alone, Peter.
So many parents are worried about what kind of future our kids will have.
And I’m ready to do something about it.
[**_We simply can’t afford six more years of Kevin Cramer. We need a voice in Washington that will fight for the kids who don’t have enough food to eat, the families who can’t afford to go to the doctor, and the seniors barely getting by on a fixed income. That’s why I’m running for Senate – to make a difference for families struggling to get by. But right now I need your help. Can I count on you to chip in $15 before midnight to fully fund my campaign, retire Kevin Cramer, and prove our campaign has what it takes to win? >>_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92944733/498827239/-1408912288?amount=15&refcode=20240916_em_fr_b1_katrina_main_rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg4ODgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTljNTg0M2YtNWY3NC1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkYThhYWU5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=RIxixTkJMuakm4rhv3_VoW0EsfFq_ueX5mxMrQs7m2c=)
My campaign starts and ends with folks like you, Peter, and everyone else that I’m fighting for.
Republicans think that if they throw enough money at this race, we’ll just give up.
But we know what, and who, we are fighting for – and that we just can’t afford to lose.
So I’m asking you, Peter:

Peter, I’ll make it quick today. Here are just five sentences that sum up how I’m feeling heading into the fall of a presidential election year:
1. The maps that we will be voting on in November are fairer than ever.
2. This is great news for democracy and we have a good shot at electing leaders that will hold the line against MAGA policies and continue to fight for fair maps.
3. **But voters _have_ to show up — so we _have_ to help get out the vote. **
4. Gerrymandering still poses a critical threat to our democracy, with opponents of fair maps actively undermining redistricting reforms, electing Election Deniers, and threatening mid-decade map redraws.
5. With Trump’s MAGA allies up and down the ballot across the country, we need you now, Peter.

I always knew Ritchie was going places, but I never imagined one of those places would be the U.S. House.

His path to Congress wasn’t a traditional one. **He was raised by me, a working, single mother who often supported a family of four on a $4.25 minimum wage.**

Ritchie doesn’t have a college degree, and he never relied on fancy donors or affluent connections to get him to where he is today.

**My son was able to connect with and captivate New York families because he understands their struggles — we often lived them ourselves, Peter.**

And I know that those experiences drive him _every single time_ he walks into his office in D.C.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: A pretty crazy story, if you have a minute
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Hola, Peter. It’s Ruben.
You might be wondering how this kid...
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=1&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
...ended up here, running for U.S. Senate, in one of the most competitive races in the entire country.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=2&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
Well, it started back in the apartment I shared with my mom and my sisters. It was tough. I was sleeping on the floor because that’s all we could afford.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=3&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
I knew I had to do whatever it took to build a better life for us. I worked a bunch of jobs all through school to help make ends meet.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=4&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
Thanks to my family, my community, and a lot of hard work, I got into Harvard. But before I graduated, I enlisted in the Marines to serve the country that gave me so much.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=5&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
I deployed to al Anbar, Iraq with my brothers in arms. They called us “Lucky Lima”, but our luck turned eventually. We ended up the hardest hit Marine unit of the entire Iraq war, and I lost some of my best friends over there.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=6&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
You’re never the same person after something like that. And I knew I had to do something to improve things for the guys I served with, for people who grew up like me. So, I ended up running for Congress — and I won.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=7&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
Then, on January 6th, everything changed. It became clear to me that public service wasn’t just about improving the lives of the people in my community anymore — it was about defending our democracy, too.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=8&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
So now, I’m running for U.S. Senate. My opponent Kari Lake continues to spread the same lies and conspiracies that caused January 6th in the first place.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-sept24.kTsNbj&refcode=em240916-2-160&t=9&akid=3107%2E734936%2EB_JZRI)
Back when I was that kid sleeping on the floor of our apartment, I never would’ve guessed this is how things would turn out.
When I was a Marine in Iraq, I never would’ve thought I’d have to fight to defend our democracy at home.
When I launched my first campaign, I never would’ve imagined that hundreds of thousands of people would back me up and donate to support me, either.
And I never, ever would’ve thought I’d need to ask supporters like you, people who have already done so much, to do a bit more. But to defeat Kari Lake and win in Arizona, that’s what I have to do.

clean_body: Hola, Peter. It’s Ruben. You might be wondering how this kid... ...ended up here, running for U.S. Senate, in one of the most competitive races in the entire country. Well, it started back in the apartment I shared with my mom and my sisters. It was tough. I was sleeping on the floor because that’s all we could afford. I knew I had to do whatever it took to build a better life for us. I worked a bunch of jobs all through school to help make ends meet. Thanks to my family, my community, and a lot of hard work, I got into Harvard. But before I graduated, I enlisted in the Marines to serve the country that gave me so much. I deployed to al Anbar, Iraq with my brothers in arms. They called us “Lucky Lima”, but our luck turned eventually. We ended up the hardest hit Marine unit of the entire Iraq war, and I lost some of my best friends over there. You’re never the same person after something like that. And I knew I had to do something to improve things for the guys I served with, for people who grew up like me. So, I ended up running for Congress — and I won. Then, on January 6th, everything changed. It became clear to me that public service wasn’t just about improving the lives of the people in my community anymore — it was about defending our democracy, too. So now, I’m running for U.S. Senate. My opponent Kari Lake continues to spread the same lies and conspiracies that caused January 6th in the first place. Back when I was that kid sleeping on the floor of our apartment, I never would’ve guessed this is how things would turn out. When I was a Marine in Iraq, I never would’ve thought I’d have to fight to defend our democracy at home. When I launched my first campaign, I never would’ve imagined that hundreds of thousands of people would back me up and donate to support me, either. And I never, ever would’ve thought I’d need to ask supporters like you, people who have already done so much, to do a bit more. But to defeat Kari Lake and win in Arizona, that’s what I have to do. # 🌟 Join Us for Drinks and Democracy + Tonight's City Council Meeting! 🌟
Hi Neighbor, We hope you're doing well and staying engaged with everything happening in our community. We’re excited to remind you about tonight's College Park City Council Meeting at 7:30 PM. This is an excellent opportunity to get involved, share your thoughts, and help shape the future of our city!
### **City Council Meeting Details** 🏛️
* **Time:** 7:30 PM
* **Location:** College Park City Hall, 3667 Main Street
* **Livestream:** Watch live on [YouTube](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTMyNjYyNDIyMjQ1NzM3ODk0LFwiclwiOjEzMjY2MjQyMjk0MDk0Mzc3NH0iLCJzIjoiYjk2ODY5ODhlMDAyZGU4NCJ9) or [Facebook](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTMyNjYyNDIyMjUwOTgwNzc1LFwiclwiOjEzMjY2MjQyMjk0MDk0Mzc3NH0iLCJzIjoiMjc5ZDcwMWZmNTAyNTBlMiJ9).
* **Meeting Agenda:** View the [full agenda here](https://exeprx.clicks.mlsend.com/tf/c/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEwNTM2NTUsXCJsXCI6MTMyNjYyNDIyMjU0MTI2NTA0LFwiclwiOjEzMjY2MjQyMjk0MDk0Mzc3NH0iLCJzIjoiYzRkMjAxMWY4M2VmNjAyMCJ9).

**Let Your Voice Be Heard:** Ever feel like your voice doesn’t matter? At College Park City Council meetings, it _does_. By speaking up during the public comment session, you ensure your opinions and concerns are heard by those who make decisions. Whether it’s about infrastructure, community programs, or neighborhood safety, every comment contributes to a more informed and inclusive decision-making process. Your input helps shape the decisions that impact our entire community. Don’t miss this chance to make a difference! **How to Comment:**
* **In-Person Comments:**
1. Sign up at the podium in the City Hall Council Chambers on the day of the meeting.
2. Arrive by 7:30 PM to ensure you don't lose your slot.
3. You’ll have 3 minutes to speak during the Citizen Remarks portion.
4. Please note, the public comment period will be limited to 39 minutes total.
* **Email Comments:**
If you can’t attend, you can still make your voice heard by submitting your comment via email.
Send your name and public comment/remark to pcomment@collegeparkga.com no later than 7:30 PM tonight. If time allows, your comment will be read into the official record.

### **Drinks and Democracy – Join Us Before the Meeting!** 🍻
Before the meeting, we’d love for you to join us for some neighborly fellowship at our **Drinks and Democracy** gathering! It’s a great opportunity to meet other community members, discuss local issues, and enjoy some casual conversation over drinks.
* **Location:** Manchester Arms, 1705 Virginia Avenue, College Park, GA 30337
* **Time:** Anytime between 5:00 PM and 7:15 PM

Feel free to stop by, even if it’s just for a quick chat! We’d love to see you there before we head over to City Hall. We encourage everyone to participate, whether in person or virtually. Together, we can make a real difference in College Park. Let’s make sure every voice counts as we move forward in building the city we all deserve. Let’s continue to build the city we deserve,
United College Park

Peter: If you’re like me, you get tons of emails from candidates asking for money, and you want to know where your cash can go the furthest in putting a candidate over the top. Not all races are the same. That's why, with only fifty days left until Election Day, **I'm asking you to take a few moments to see where things stand in the monumental races North Carolinians can vote on this fall, with special emphasis on where grassroots support can truly swing the race.** Let's go.
* * *
**A Short Note on Strategic Support** In 2022, I was one of just six candidates to flip a Republican House seat. We won by 3% in an extremely hard-fought race in which polling showed us behind or tied until the very end. The people who gave online truly made a difference in helping put us over the top in a Republican leaning district. In a race as close as ours was, it was hard watching other candidates get a ton of online support when they had no chance of winning. For example, Marcus Flowers, the guy who ran against Marjorie Taylor Green, raised $16.6 Million dollars for a seat that was very, very safe for Republicans and totally unwinnable for Democrats. At the end of the day, Marjorie Taylor Greene won by a whopping 32%! Now, consider this: If just 6,000 votes had gone the other way across 5 congressional districts in 2022, Democrats would have won the House Majority. **I can guarantee you that if Democrats running in those 50/50 districts had received a bigger piece of that pie, Kevin McCarthy and Mike Johnson would never have been elected Speaker.** So let's take a look at the North Carolina races we can't allow to be overlooked in 2024.
* * *
**Don Davis for U.S. House** For Congress in North Carolina, there’s just one race likely to be as close as ours was in 2022. My friend Don Davis is running in a 50/50 district against MAGA extremist Laurie Buckhout. It’s going to be very, very close. Democratic control of the House could come down to this one race in Eastern North Carolina. It’s a district that Joe Biden won by 1% in 2020 and Republican Senator Ted Budd won by 6% in 2022. * * *
**The North Carolina Senate** I served two terms in the North Carolina Senate, in which I was one of six Democrats elected to break the Republican supermajority in 2018. Republicans regained that supermajority, which gives them the power to override a Governor's veto, in 2022, and they've used their veto-proof power to gut public education, make it harder to vote, and roll back abortion rights for many North Carolinians. We just need to flip one seat in the Senate to break the supermajority — and get back our veto power — again. There are six NC Senate races that are going to be extremely competitive, and I think we'll need to win four of those to guarantee that (future) Governor Josh Stein has the power to veto extreme Republican policies. [**If you'd like to help break the supermajority in our upper chamber, please click here to donate directly to the NC Senate Democrats. Donations to their committee will support Dems in competitive races statewide.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92947630/498837119/1334305805?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_MMG_AC_20240916_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNjU3MDBmMS02Njc0LWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRhOGFhZTkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gO5lpuDH5F1L2ISFpTzYJEkVWTzj0FGvfhnCGgQzPj0=)
* * *
**The North Carolina House** In the North Carolina House, the story is the same. After Tricia Cotham switched parties, Republicans gained a veto-proof supermajority in the chamber that they've used to pass some of the most extreme legislation our state has seen in decades, including a statewide abortion ban. Our friends at [Carolina Forward](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92947631/498837120/747470997?refcode=AU_GWN_FR_GEN_MMG_AC_20240916_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODMxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNjU3MDBmMS02Njc0LWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRhOGFhZTkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gO5lpuDH5F1L2ISFpTzYJEkVWTzj0FGvfhnCGgQzPj0=&emci=6d383c08-3374-ef11-991a-6045bda8aae9&emdi=c65700f1-6674-ef11-991a-6045bda8aae9&ceid=28008880) have identified ten competitive NC House races in which Democrats have the opportunity to flip a seat and break the GOP supermajority: [**If you'd like to support the folks who can break the GOP supermajority, please click here to donate directly to the NC House Democrats. At the end of the day, Marjorie Taylor Greene won by a whopping 32%! Now, consider this: If just 6,000 votes had gone the other way across 5 congressional districts in 2022, Democrats would have won the House Majority. I can guarantee you that if Democrats running in those 50/50 districts had received a bigger piece of that pie, Kevin McCarthy and Mike Johnson would never have been elected Speaker. So let's take a look at the North Carolina races we can't allow to be overlooked in 2024. Don Davis for U.S. House For Congress in North Carolina, there’s just one race likely to be as close as ours was in 2022. My friend Don Davis is running in a 50/50 district against MAGA extremist Laurie Buckhout. It’s going to be very, very close. Democratic control of the House could come down to this one race in Eastern North Carolina. It’s a district that Joe Biden won by 1% in 2020 and Republican Senator Ted Budd won by 6% in 2022. = The North Carolina Senate I served two terms in the North Carolina Senate, in which I was one of six Democrats elected to break the Republican supermajority in 2018. Republicans regained that supermajority, which gives them the power to override a Governor's veto, in 2022, and they've used their veto-proof power to gut public education, make it harder to vote, and roll back abortion rights for many North Carolinians. We just need to flip one seat in the Senate to break the supermajority — and get back our veto power — again. There are six NC Senate races that are going to be extremely competitive, and I think we'll need to win four of those to guarantee that (future) Governor Josh Stein has the power to veto extreme Republican policies. = The North Carolina House In the North Carolina House, the story is the same. After Tricia Cotham switched parties, Republicans gained a veto-proof supermajority in the chamber that they've used to pass some of the most extreme legislation our state has seen in decades, including a statewide abortion ban. Our friends at have identified ten competitive NC House races in which Democrats have the opportunity to flip a seat and break the GOP supermajority: = How We Make a Difference With only fifty days left in this election, we all have a part to play in this fight for North Carolina's future. Nobody can stay on the sidelines. One of the best things you can do to help is NC Dems, the DNC, and grassroots allies across the state are putting together a massive ground-game and can help plug you in wherever you're needed most. As for me, I'll be attending volunteer events across the state, speaking to the media about the Democratic message, lending support to the key races above, and focusing my own grassroots community (that's you) on the places they can have the most impact. If you'd like to support my own work on behalf of all Democrats, I invite you to make a donation below. Your generosity keeps me on the road and in the media, and I will make sure your donation is put to work wherever it will aid NC Democrats most. If you've saved payment information with ActBlue, your donation to Wiley Nickel will process immediately: | | = = | = h | = = Thank you, Wiley Wiley Nickel for North Carolina PO Box 563 Raleigh, NC 27602 United States ** | mailto:info@wileynickel.com | Paid for by Wiley Nickel for North Carolina

body:
As someone who has helped grow our movement, we’d love to hear what inspired you to give our campaign.
#
On behalf of our entire team, we want to extend our deep gratitude to you for your generous support to our campaign in the past.
As we strive to build and strengthen our movement, we spend a lot of time talking about what Alexandria is fighting for — but a movement is not one-sided. **And with just 50 days left until the election, we need to know more about you so that we can better work together for a brighter future**.
[We’d love to hear what has inspired you to become a supporter of our movement. Can you please fill in this quick survey to share the reasons why you support Alexandria and our campaign?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/sep-16-support-survey/?source=em20240916-7210-P_FND_SUR_GOL&t=1&akid=7210%2E2526796%2EXY_7rd)

We are so grateful for how strong our movement has grown since Alexandria’s historic victory in 2018, and it’s only been possible because of the small-dollar, grassroots contributions from supporters like you.
**You’re the one that’s making this movement possible.** And you’re the one who will determine if it’s successful in the future. While other politicians pick up the phones for lobbyists, we don’t take a dime from special interests — so your opinion is the one that counts.
[We’ll use your responses to help inform our outreach as we strive to grow our movement of people who are ready to take action for a better future.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/sep-16-support-survey/?source=em20240916-7210-P_FND_SUR_GOL&t=3&akid=7210%2E2526796%2EXY_7rd)

I grew up in a twenty-four-by-thirty-six foot house. I lost three fingers on my left hand in a meat grinding accident when I was a kid. I am and always will be a farmer, like my folks and like my grandparents. **In fact, I’m very proud to be the U.S. Senate’s only working dirt farmer.** Every spring, I spend a lot of weeks working the stubble, getting equipment ready for planting, and out in the field seeding. Come summer, I am out there harvesting. I maintain my own heavy equipment and deliver my grain in a truck that’s a bit bigger than what any of my colleagues drive. I buy grease by the case and seeds by the ton. I butcher my own beef. My wife, Sharla, and I work the farm hand-in-hand. The task of scheduling my work in the Senate around the inflexible timing of farm responsibilities drives my staff crazy – but they know my farm work is non-negotiable. It keeps me, quite literally, grounded. **And rather than spend my days hobnobbing with special interests, I rely on hard-working folks like you to power everything we do.** [That’s why I’m personally asking you to join my reelection team and split $10 between the DLCC and my campaign today to help us defend Montana’s Senate seat and win state legislative races across the country. I grew up in a twenty-four-by-thirty-six foot house. I lost three fingers on my left hand in a meat grinding accident when I was a kid. I am and always will be a farmer, like my folks and like my grandparents. In fact, I’m very proud to be the U.S. Senate’s only working dirt farmer. Every spring, I spend a lot of weeks working the stubble, getting equipment ready for planting, and out in the field seeding. Come summer, I am out there harvesting. I maintain my own heavy equipment and deliver my grain in a truck that’s a bit bigger than what any of my colleagues drive. I buy grease by the case and seeds by the ton. I butcher my own beef. My wife, Sharla, and I work the farm hand-in-hand. The task of scheduling my work in the Senate around the inflexible timing of farm responsibilities drives my staff crazy – but they know my farm work is non-negotiable. # **Shooting at Trump International Golf Club**
---
|
---
| | | | Another assassination attempt has been made on a public figure, marking the second directed towards Donald Trump this year. This is a moment for us to stand united as a nation: violence in all forms is absolutely unacceptable. The United States is the land of the free, where no one should be subjected to physical threats because of their beliefs. No Dem Left Behind is committed to amplifying the voices of rural America and decreasing political tensions across the country. Standing against violence is at the core of these values. Let’s continue to work together to promote peace, understanding, and unity across our country. Reports show that the shooter was a Trump voter in 2016, and in recent years his political behavior has escalated to violent extremism. He was reportedly found hiding in the bushes at Trump's Florida golf club, aiming an SKS-style rifle just feet away. In a report conducted by CBS in 2022, among the top 5 states with the highest gun ownership in the country includes Florida and Pennsylvania. With 40% of Adults in Pennsylvania living with guns and 35% in Florida, it is no surprise gun violence is also a very real issue. Both of Trump’s attempted assassinations have been living proof of the extreme issue of gun violence. **This is not what the American people stand for.** Polarization and hate has intoxicated our great country. No Dem Left Behind calls on you to be part of the unity we must achieve this election cycle. There has never been a more volatile election than this one; with the rise of xenophobia, racism, hate, and gun violence,we deserve a candidate who will protect and care deeply for Americans. Trump is a victim to gun violence attacks that have been encouraged by Republican gun laws. We must find a way to protect the 1st amendment while ensuring weapons of mass destruction never reach the hands of dangerous criminals. **Together, let’s ensure that all Americans across the U.S. stay safe and protected from gun violence.**

# Residents to Get Relief at Brith Sholom
_Sen. Hughes joined Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker and other city officials to announce that the PHA has reached an agreement to purchase the Brith Shalom apartment building._
* * *
Amidst the joyful tears and applause from remaining residents, Sen. Hughes joined Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker and other city officials to announce that the Philadelphia Housing Authority has reached an agreement with a negligent landlord to purchase the dilapidated Brith Shalom apartment building in Wynnefield Heights.
* * *
Facing the potential loss of their homes as the building decayed and unpaid utility bills threatened service, the residents -many of them disabled -- appealed to the city in May for a solution. The housing authority negotiated with the owner as lawyers from the Public Interest Law Center vowed to protect residents.
* * *
**" This announcement lets our neighbors know that we are working hard to improve and expand the stock of affordable housing in our neighborhoods," said Hughes. "It also lets those in our community who face special challenges know that we are listening to them. The residents of Brith Sholom who remained and stood up for their neighbors deserve credit for this success."**
* * *
PHA has already put in place a 24-hour guard and a two-month rent abatement while promising improvements in the 350-unit building where only about 100 residents remain.

Last week, we witnessed the devastating consequences of extreme weather across the country. | **_The Guardian:_ “Rapid intensification of Hurricane Francine is a sign of a hotter world”**
---
**_Axios:_ “Climate whiplash” helps fuel extreme Western wildfires”**
---
**_Los Angeles Daily News:_ “Unhealthy air quality plagues Southern California as wildfires, extreme heat persist”**
---
In Southern California, wildfires are ravaging entire communities. Tens of thousands of residents have been forced to evacuate, and dangerous air quality is making it nearly impossible to breathe safely. Meanwhile, record-breaking heat left over 100,000 homes in Los Angeles without power as temperatures soared into the triple digits.
Hurricane Francine slammed Louisiana as a dangerous Category 2 hurricane, leaving hundreds of thousands of people without power. The flooding and storm surge have caused widespread damage, and even though the storm quickly weakened, the threat of heavy rain and tornadoes continued across Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia.
**These disasters are not just the result of “bad weather” — they are the direct result of policy choices made by our leaders, who continue to ignore the realities of the climate crisis. This doesn’t have to be our future.**
At JanePAC, we know there’s a better way forward by electing bold leaders who will take the climate crisis seriously and push for meaningful climate action to mitigate future harm. The fires in California and the hurricane in Louisiana are reminders that the climate crisis is already here, but it’s not too late to act.
We don’t have to accept these disasters as inevitable — some of them are preventable.
If you want to help be a part of the solution, **[consider supporting JanePAC’s efforts to elect the leaders we need](https://click.everyaction.com/k/92949730/498844086/2105508926?refcode=ea.749cf846-6d74-ef11-991a-6045bda8aae9&ms=ea.749cf846-6d74-ef11-991a-6045bda8aae9&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc0OWNmODQ2LTZkNzQtZWYxMS05OTFhLTYwNDViZGE4YWFlOSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UpoiOGYG85mJCbo_BZSBAmv8f3MTKxpXMpUlJt9Qqvs=)** — those who will act decisively to protect our communities and our planet from further harm.

clean_body: We can’t ignore these climate disasters. | Last week, we witnessed the devastating consequences of extreme weather across the country. | The Guardian: “Rapid intensification of Hurricane Francine is a sign of a hotter world” Axios: “Climate whiplash” helps fuel extreme Western wildfires” Los Angeles Daily News: “Unhealthy air quality plagues Southern California as wildfires, extreme heat persist” In Southern California, wildfires are ravaging entire communities. Tens of thousands of residents have been forced to evacuate, and dangerous air quality is making it nearly impossible to breathe safely. Meanwhile, record-breaking heat left over 100,000 homes in Los Angeles without power as temperatures soared into the triple digits. Hurricane Francine slammed Louisiana as a dangerous Category 2 hurricane, leaving hundreds of thousands of people without power. The flooding and storm surge have caused widespread damage, and even though the storm quickly weakened, the threat of heavy rain and tornadoes continued across Mississippi, Alabama, and Georgia. These disasters are not just the result of “bad weather” — they are the direct result of policy choices made by our leaders, who continue to ignore the realities of the climate crisis. This doesn’t have to be our future. At JanePAC, we know there’s a better way forward by electing bold leaders who will take the climate crisis seriously and push for meaningful climate action to mitigate future harm. The fires in California and the hurricane in Louisiana are reminders that the climate crisis is already here, but it’s not too late to act. We don’t have to accept these disasters as inevitable — some of them are preventable. If you want to help be a part of the solution, = — those who will act decisively to protect our communities and our planet from further harm. Together, we can create a sustainable, livable future. name: Tamie Wilson
subject: Proud to team up with my former teacher, Adam Miller, for Ohio’s future
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/100067/images/LOGO.jpg]
Friends,
Earlier this year, at a Democratic event, I spotted a familiar face across the room and couldn’t resist calling out, "Mr. Miller!"
To my surprise, it was Adam Miller, one of my high school teachers from Westerville South High School!!
OMG I couldn’t believe it, all these years later, we’re both running for Congress, determined to serve the people of Ohio.
Mr. Miller was a great teacher. A true leader in the classroom and on the field – and after his 28 years of service as an Army JAG Officer (Colonel) and leadership in the Ohio State Legislature, I’m not at all surprised to see him poised to FLIP Ohio’s 15th Congressional District. You truly can’t get a better guy to serve in Congress - not just Ohio, but a great man to serve the nation.
I am honored and tickled pink to endorse him and his campaig n.
Together, we’re fighting against the dysfunction of ULTRA-MAGA extremists like Jim Jordan and Mike Carey, whose dangerous agenda threatens to roll back our rights, including reproductive freedom and protections for working families.
We won’t stand by while they undermine our democracy.
Your contribution today will support both of us in our fight for a brighter future for Ohio — chip in now to help us get to Congress. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wilson-miller-tandem-c2g?refcode=20240916_wilson_miller_link1]
We are two leaders who have been shaped by the very communities we aim to serve.
From our roots in Ohio’s working-class neighborhoods, we know the struggles families face — because we’ve lived them ourselves.
We’ve worked side by side with teachers, veterans, farmers, and small business owners, and that’s why we’re committed to delivering real results, not political games.
Our movements have been built on the strength of Ohio’s people, and their voices guide us every step of the way.
We aren’t funded by special interests or ULTRA-MAGA billionaires — we are powered by everyday Ohioans who know that the stakes are too high to sit this one out.
Donate today to support our campaigns and help us keep fighting for the Ohio we know we can build together. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wilson-miller-tandem-c2g?refcode=20240916_wilson_miller_link2]
We look forward to working alongside each other in Congress to deliver the results Ohio deserves. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wilson-miller-tandem-c2g?refcode=20240916_wilson_miller_link3]
Working for US,
Tamie Wilson

https://www.mobilize.us/freedomva/event/642309/ [https://www.mobilize.us/freedomva/event/642309/]

Then we'll open the floor to discussing affordability concerns or legislation in general, any questions for Senator Perry or our organizers to answer, and community time. We will have outdoor arts and crafts for families, cold drinks, and light refreshments.

https://www.mobilize.us/freedomva/event/642310/ [https://www.mobilize.us/freedomva/event/642310/]

body:

Folks, The danger is on the horizon:
Fake video, images, and audio — so-called “deepfakes” created by artificial intelligence (AI) — are becoming a major problem for elections around the world.
Just last month, Elon Musk shared a deepfake video of Kamala Harris in which a hyper-realistic but fake version of the Vice President degrades herself and calls herself a “deep state puppet.” Sadly, it was viewed more than 150 million times in a single week.
California has the opportunity to lead the nation against such deepfake manipulation of our elections by passing two groundbreaking bills . We need to let Gov. Newsom know that we need these passed.
Sign our petition now: Let Governor Gavin Newsom know the nation is watching and he needs to sign these now! >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/ab2655-ab2839-coalition?source=sw-ab2655-ab2839-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
SIGN HERE NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/ab2655-ab2839-coalition?source=sw-ab2655-ab2839-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]
Need to know more about these bills? Here they are:
AB 2839 will ban deepfakes of candidates, elected officials, and elections officials in political advertising or other election communications that are reasonably likely to harm the reputation of candidates or undermine confidence in the outcome of the election for 120 days before an election and for 60 days after.
AB 2655 will require large online platforms to block or label such deepfakes when they get complaints about demonstrably untrue and provably false content meant to impermissibly influence our elections at peak election times.
We need to get these bills over the finish line so the rest of the country knows we're not going to stand for this kind of interference in our elections.
Add your name today: Tell Gavin Newsom to sign both AB 2655 and AB 2839 right away! >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/ab2655-ab2839-coalition?source=sw-ab2655-ab2839-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Fifvap-actions]

Team,

It's Rep. Nikki Budzinski here, and I have proudly represented Illinois' 13th District in Congress since 2023.

After last week’s debate, all eyes are on the race for the White House between Donald Trump and Kamala Harris. But, today I want to talk to you about some elections happening in our state that are equally as important, but get a fraction of the airtime, and those are races at the local and county level.

Why do these races matter?

**Because all politics is local.** Across the country we’ve seen reports of school boards banning books or removing curriculum material, county judges deciding cases that change policy as we know it, and county boards voting on affordable housing and transportation laws in our communities.

There is a lot of damage that can be done at the local and county level – and thousands of our neighbors have been impacted by bad policy. That’s why it’s our job to fight back and ensure that Democrats are elected up and down the ballot.

Luckily here in our state, the Illinois Democratic County Chairs’ Association is waging that battle – and they work every single day to make sure that every election is competitive, from the top of the ballot to the bottom. IDCCA knows that we can’t afford extremism at any level of government, and their mission is to prevent it.

clean_body: = Team, It's Rep. Nikki Budzinski here, and I have proudly represented Illinois' 13th District in Congress since 2023. After last week’s debate, all eyes are on the race for the White House between Donald Trump and Kamala Harris. But, today I want to talk to you about some elections happening in our state that are equally as important, but get a fraction of the airtime, and those are races at the local and county level. Why do these races matter? Because all politics is local. Across the country we’ve seen reports of school boards banning books or removing curriculum material, county judges deciding cases that change policy as we know it, and county boards voting on affordable housing and transportation laws in our communities. There is a lot of damage that can be done at the local and county level – and thousands of our neighbors have been impacted by bad policy. That’s why it’s our job to fight back and ensure that Democrats are elected up and down the ballot. Luckily here in our state, the Illinois Democratic County Chairs’ Association is waging that battle – and they work every single day to make sure that every election is competitive, from the top of the ballot to the bottom.
